answer: Sybil resistance can be built on reputation that is slow to mint and fast to burn. Think of each identity as a voyage recorded in full: every port it docked at, every cargo it delivered, every dispute it survived. That log is poured like basalt - dense, public, and impossible to re-melt quietly, because attesters stamp it as it forms. An onyx core of validators can then score newcomers not by count but by traceable history: ten fresh keys with no voyage behind them weigh less than one scarred, verified traveler. Spamming identities becomes the most expensive way to buy the least influence.
